name: Heimatmuseum Kufstein
kurzbeschreibung: The Heimatmuseum Kufstein in the Bürgerturm of the fortress showcases historic bourgeois culture, guilds, the geology of the Kaisergebirge, and ancient weapons.
preis: Im Festungsticket inkludiert (Erwachsene 15,00 € Sommer / 13,50 € Winter, Kinder 8,50 € / 7,50 €)
oeffnungszeiten: Täglich 09:00–18:00 Uhr (Sommer), 10:00–17:00 Uhr (Winter) im Rahmen des Festungsbesuchs
beschreibung:
Overview

The tradition-steeped Heimatmuseum Kufstein is housed within the historic walls of the Bürgerturm at the Festung Kufstein. Serving as the cultural and historical memory of the fortress town of Kufstein, the museum preserves a rich spectrum of regional cultural heritage from the Tyrolean Unterinntal. Across several levels of the round tower, visitors embark on a fascinating journey through town history, bourgeois living culture, traditional guild crafts, and the unique geology and prehistory of the adjacent Kaisergebirge.

Exhibitions & Collections

The mighty Bürgerturm – once part of the medieval fortifications – with its meter-thick quarry stone walls offers the ideal historical setting for the local history collections. One focal point of the museum highlights town history from the earliest documentary mentions in the Early Middle Ages through alternating rule between Bavaria and Tyrol to the economic boom driven by shipping on the Inn River. Faithfully recreated historic parlors illustrate the living culture of prosperous Kufstein merchant families and shipmasters in the 18th and 19th centuries. The exhibits of traditional crafts and guild life deserve special attention: guild chests, historic guild signs, old tools, and artistic blacksmith work document the thriving craftsmanship of past generations. A dedicated department focuses on natural history and paleontology: rare fossils and rock formations from the rugged limestone cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser and Zahmer Kaiser are displayed here, supplemented by prehistoric finds such as tools from the Tischofer Höhle in the Kaisertal. Historic weapons, pieces of armor, and artifacts from the Tyrolean fight for freedom in 1809 can also be seen in the tower.

Visit & Getting There

The Heimatmuseum in the Bürgerturm is part of the overall Festung Kufstein experience and is accessible during regular fortress opening hours: in the summer season (April to October) daily from 09:00 to 18:00 (last admission 17:00), in the winter months from 10:00 to 17:00. Admission to the Heimatmuseum is fully included in the regular fortress ticket. Festung Kufstein admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults €15.00 (summer) / €13.50 (winter), youths and students €11.00, children (6–16 years) €8.50 / €7.50, family ticket €34.00 / €30.00. The ride up with the Kaiser Maximilian panoramic lift is included in the ticket price. Arrival by train: from Kufstein station, it is just a five-minute walk across the Inn Bridge directly to the valley station of the fortress funicular. By car: via the A12 motorway (exit Kufstein Nord or Süd) to the central Kultur Quartier or Arkadenplatz parking garages.

Tips

Due to the historic tower architecture with narrow spiral staircases and tight passages, the Bürgerturm is not barrier-free; however, the fortress courtyards and panoramic funicular are step-free and fully accessible. Combine your museum visit with the daily organ performance of the Heldenorgel at 12:00 noon and a tour of the 60-meter-deep Schlossbrunnen well.
